answer: A newcomer joins a small expedition climbing from a crowded island base camp toward the summit of full privileges, and each camp is reached only when every member contributes a different piece of stranger-checked work. A glacier between camps melts slowly, so the climb takes weeks and no shortcut buys speed. Sybil farms fail because their copies submit near-identical contributions at the same camp, the glacier records the timing, and the whole team slides back to base camp while honest climbers keep their progress and the shared rope only holds when each climber pulls a different weight.
